title: The Mountains Dissolve…
text:
The mountains dissolve,

the cattle have been lost;

the sun returns to its forge:

the whole world flees away.


The orchard is being erased,

the farm has sunk from sight,

and my mountain range submerges

its summit and its living cry.


Creatures slip sideways

toward oblivion,

and we too go rolling

into the night, my child.
editorial_note: The landscape's disappearance is kept active and progressive, widening the lullaby into an apocalyptic dusk.

title: Little Lamb
text:
Little lamb of mine,

silent softness:

my breast is your grotto,

velveted with moss.


Little body, white,

a slice of moon:

I have forgotten everything

to become your cradle.


I forgot the world,

and of myself I feel

nothing but the living breast

with which I sustain you.


And all I know of myself

is that you rest in me.

Your feast, my child,

has put all feasts out.
editorial_note: Mistral's diminutives become tactile intimacy; the final apagó keeps both extinguishing and surpassing.

title: Riches
text:
I have faithful happiness

and happiness lost:

one like a rose,

the other like a thorn.

What they stole from me

did not dispossess me;

I have faithful happiness

and happiness lost,

and I am rich in purple

and in melancholy.

Oh, how loving is the rose,

and how beloved the thorn!

Like the double outline

of twin fruits,

I have faithful happiness

and happiness lost.
editorial_note: Dicha is kept as happiness rather than luck; faithful and lost sustain the poem's paradoxical wealth.

title: If Only You Will Sleep
text:
The red rose

picked yesterday;

the fire and cinnamon

they call carnation;


the oven-baked bread

of anise and honey,

and the fish in the glass bowl

that sets it burning:


all of it yours,

little son of woman,

if only you will consent

to sleep at last.


The rose, I say;

I say the carnation.

The fruit, I say,

and I say the honey;


and the fish made of light,

and more and still more too,

if only you will sleep

until daybreak!
editorial_note: The mother's escalating promises retain their nursery incantation and gently exasperated bargain.

title: She Who Was a Girl of Wax…
text:
She who was a girl of wax—

but she was not a girl of wax,

she was a sheaf standing on the threshing floor.

But she was not a sheaf,

but the stiff flower of the marvel.

Nor was she the flower, but rather

a little ray of sunlight stuck to the windowpane.

She was not even a little ray of sunlight:

she was a speck of straw inside my eyes.


Come close and see how I have wholly lost,

inside this enormous tear, my true celebration!
editorial_note: The chain of transformations stays breathless and childlike; maravilla remains marvel to preserve flower and wonder at once.

title: Clinging to Me
text:
Little fleece of my flesh,

woven within my womb,

little fleece chilled by the cold,

sleep now, clinging to me!


The partridge sleeps in clover,

listening to its heartbeat:

let my breathing not disturb you;

sleep now, clinging to me!


Little trembling blade of grass,

astonished to be alive,

do not loosen from my breast:

sleep now, clinging to me!


I who have lost everything

now tremble even in sleep.

Do not slip out of my arm:

sleep now, clinging to me!
editorial_note: The maternal refrain is kept bodily and urgent; fleece carries warmth, fragility, and shared flesh.

title: Night
text:
So that you may sleep, my child,

the sunset burns no more:

nothing shines now but the dew,

nothing is whiter than my face.


So that you may sleep, my child,

the road has fallen silent:

no one moans except the river;

nothing exists except me.


The plain has drowned in mist.

The blue sigh has drawn in.

Stillness has come to rest,

like a hand upon the world.


I did not rock only

my child inside my song:

the cradle's back-and-forth

was lulling Earth to sleep…
editorial_note: The translation follows the lullaby's narrowing hush and then restores its cosmic reach in the final cradle motion.

title: Sleep, My Child…
text:
Sleep now, my child,

sleep with a smile,

for the ring of stars

is rocking you.


You delighted in the light

and you were happy.

You had every good thing

when you had me.


Sleep now, my child,

sleep with a smile,

for loving Earth

is rocking you.


You gazed upon the burning

crimson rose.

You embraced the world:

you embraced me.


Sleep now, my child,

sleep with a smile,

for it is God in the darkness

who is rocking you.
editorial_note: The repeated rocking joins mother, Earth, stars, and God in the same circular lullaby.
